display.title: The King in the Field: The Month of Elul
display.summary_short: In Elul, Hashem is like a king who comes out to the field to greet his people and grant their requests: the Alter Rebbe's famous parable, told for children.
display.summary_long: A short Elul talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi asks children to picture a king returning to his palace: everyone goes out to the fields to greet him, and there anyone can approach him face to face, and he welcomes them all with a smiling face and grants their requests. This, he explains, is the month of Elul, as the Alter Rebbe writes in Likkutei Torah: Hashem is like the King in the field, closer and more available than at any other time of year. Elul is the month of mercy, when Hashem gladly accepts those who return to Him wholeheartedly. So now is the time to examine our thoughts, be careful with our words and weigh our deeds, and to ask for the greatest wish of all, Moshiach now, so that we greet Hashem in the new Beis HaMikdash in Yerushalayim in the coming year.
display.lesson: In Elul Hashem is close and ready to listen, so use the month to improve your thoughts, words and deeds and ask Him for what you need.
